jp-1FK1.title: Plants: sugarcane
jp-1FK1.summary: Sugarcane is almost only on the islands of southern Kyushu and Okinawa.

jp-1dQi.title: Bollard: thick, octagon top, two yellow stripes
jp-1dQi.summary: Like the Tohoku one: thick, white, octagonal reflector, but with two yellow stripes underneath. This is the Akita version.

jp-224S.title: Pole: tuning-fork top with thin wire
jp-224S.summary: A tuning-fork pole top with a thin wire and a horizontal bar below is common in Kansai.

jp-28LV.title: Pole: basic thin snow pole
jp-28LV.summary: In northern Chugoku, thin snow poles, extended or contracted, are the usual bollard. Also sometimes in Iwate.

jp-33NM.title: Guardrail: red and yellow striped end stickers
jp-33NM.summary: Red-and-yellow striped stickers on guardrail ends are common across Chugoku except Yamaguchi, and rarely in Niigata.

jp-3Yji.title: Pole: tent-shaped top, sides filled in
jp-3Yji.summary: A pole top with two filled-in sides shaped like a tent is common in Hokuriku.

jp-5BgJ.title: Plants: Chinese silver grass, abundant on Kyushu
jp-5BgJ.summary: Chinese silver grass is very abundant on Kyushu but also appears elsewhere, notably in Niigata, Yamagata and Akita. Use with care.

jp-5e4A.title: Plants: rice paddies, mostly north of Tokyo
jp-5e4A.summary: Rice is mainly grown north of Tokyo, looks like grass when growing, shows brown husks at harvest, and is often planted in water beds. Tohoku, Chubu, Kanto and Hokkaido grow most of it.

jp-6557.title: Pole: top with four thin skinny bars
jp-6557.summary: A pole top with four thin, skinny bars is common in Chugoku.

jp-6R3b.title: Coverage: little winter coverage in Hokkaido
jp-6R3b.summary: Hokkaido has very little winter and snow coverage, so unless you are sure, don't guess it. Other small amounts of coverage are mainly in the southern half.

jp-72uf.title: Pole: round concrete with screw-like steps
jp-72uf.summary: Round concrete poles with screw-like extensions, usually with electrical plates, guy wires or reflectors attached. Key objects for finding the region.

jp-8hcH.title: Pole: tuning-fork top with long top bar
jp-8hcH.summary: A tuning-fork pole top with a long top bar sticking out at each end and bars below it is mostly Kanto.

jp-9fGX.title: Pole: small 90-degree angled arm
jp-9fGX.summary: Smaller attachments with a 90-degree angle are common on poles in Shikoku.

jp-EIwA.title: Guardrail: simple white
jp-EIwA.summary: Guardrails are generally simple and white.

jp-FLxL.title: Pole: transformer on plus-shaped bar or two bars
jp-FLxL.summary: In Hokkaido, poles have a plus-shaped bar on the side, or a transformer on two bars. Several transformers are usually on the sides of a square. The Kanto one may also use two bars, but Hokkaido never has a wooden plate.

jp-FRiS.hide: no learnable content (only points to an external trekker resource)

jp-HTvr.title: House: kerosene tank, 'Claymore'
jp-HTvr.summary: Kerosene tanks (Claymores) get more common going north. They are abundant in Hokkaido and appear in prefectures to the south and in high mountains.

jp-HmjC.title: Plants: white birch trunks
jp-HmjC.summary: Japanese white birch grows mainly in Chubu and Hokkaido, less in Tohoku, with small patches everywhere. Japanese beech has grey, spotted bark instead.

jp-IQ4Z.title: Traffic light: vertical
jp-IQ4Z.summary: Vertical traffic lights are in Hokkaido and along the northwest coast. Horizontal ones are everywhere else.

jp-J3hs.title: Landscape: tall volcano with gentle slope
jp-J3hs.summary: Mount Fuji, the tallest mountain, has a gradual slope and often a snowy top. It can be seen from far away, so direction and distance help.

jp-JhXh.title: Sign: unique stop sign, mirrors, school crossing
jp-JhXh.summary: Three common sights: a unique stop sign, a school pedestrian crossing, and traffic mirrors at junctions.

jp-LVv4.title: Phone numbers: area codes rise going south
jp-LVv4.summary: Area codes get larger further south. Codes ending in 0, such as 0120, are usually not regional.

jp-LYWn.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image)

jp-LxRM.title: Guardrail: yellow
jp-LxRM.summary: Yellow guardrails are found in Yamaguchi.

jp-Nw5V.title: Pole: cross bar with full triangle, red numbers
jp-Nw5V.summary: In Chugoku, a cross-shaped bar in the middle of the pole on a full triangle, with long horizontal or short vertical insulators. A white sticker with red numbers is often under the transformer.

jp-O99c.title: Pole: transformer on wooden plate and two bars
jp-O99c.summary: In Kanto, transformers with two or three insulators are often on a wooden plate with two bars, or a round plate with a T-shaped bar. Hokkaido's can use two bars but never a wooden plate.

jp-PmSr.hide: no visual clue (terminology intro: islands, regions, prefectures)

jp-QJIK.title: Houses: red-tiled roofs
jp-QJIK.summary: These red-tiled roofs are most common in Chugoku, especially Hiroshima and Shimane.

jp-Qteb.title: Manhole: five-petal flower with small circles
jp-Qteb.summary: Tokyo's manhole design has a five-petal flower and many small circles around the edge.

jp-RRYf.title: Road: arrow marking the road edge under snow
jp-RRYf.summary: An arrow showing drivers where the road edge is under snow, almost only in Hokkaido. Variants: silver bolts around the border in Aomori; long and thin in Gifu; yellow-black on Highway 275; yellow-green southwest of Sapporo.

jp-SR14.title: Bollard: black stripe under the reflector
jp-SR14.summary: On Shikoku some bollards have a black stripe just under the reflector, on their own or attached to guardrails or walls.

jp-T1C7.title: Google car: low camera, big blur, black-white car
jp-T1C7.summary: The car is often black and white, rarely with an antenna. The camera sits low, so the car blur is big and the road looks wide from a low angle. Switzerland is always low-cam too, but its car is blurred out.

differs.how: Swiss car is blurred out; Japan's is visible

jp-U9cw.title: Pole: grey insulator-like blocks
jp-U9cw.summary: Grey blocks like insulators, with wires fed through, appear in Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku and Shikoku, and very rarely Hokkaido.

jp-VKyx.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image)

jp-Vpks.title: Wall: retaining walls in rural areas
jp-Vpks.summary: Retaining walls are a good clue in rural areas with little else to go on.

jp-WYsB.title: Road lines: white edges, never yellow edges
jp-WYsB.summary: Three common styles: white edges with a dashed white middle (most common), white edges with solid yellow middle, or white edges with yellow and white middle lines. Edge lines are never yellow.

jp-XLBR.title: Pole: transformer on round plate with zigzag bar
jp-XLBR.summary: In Tohoku, transformers often have square holding brackets and the Tohoku Electric logo, sometimes on a round plate with a zigzag bar, or on a square with a straight bar on top. Kansai's square has the bar at the bottom.

jp-YbtC.title: Bollard: thick, octagon reflector, yellow stripe
jp-YbtC.summary: A thick white bollard with an octagonal reflector and a yellow stripe under it, in Tohoku, also with a rectangular top. Black octagonal and rectangular versions exist on national highways and expressways, sometimes with the road number.

jp-YpAf.title: Bollard: one reflector, extendable, red stripe
jp-YpAf.summary: One reflector, extendable, with a red stripe under it, in Toyama. A second reflector or a yellow stripe instead is a different, more widespread bollard.

jp-ZAar.title: Pole: tuning-fork top with short top bar
jp-ZAar.summary: A tuning-fork pole top with a short top bar and a horizontal bar below is mostly Chubu.

jp-ZMK9.title: Pole: T-bar, transformers on opposite sides
jp-ZMK9.summary: In Okinawa, a T-shaped bar on the side of the pole with transformers on opposite sides.

jp-ZevZ.title: Pole: transformer with yellow numbers, black taps
jp-ZevZ.summary: In Chubu, transformers often have painted yellow numbers and black tap connectors, attached with a big triangle and horizontal bars or thin metal brackets.

jp-acST.title: Pole: orange arrow above the top plate
jp-acST.summary: In the Chugoku region, you may see an orange arrow above the top pole plate.

jp-c1R6.title: Pole: transformers opposite sides, 3 insulators
jp-c1R6.summary: In Kyushu, a straight bar on the side of the pole with three insulators at the end, with transformers 180 degrees apart.

jp-c2hu.title: Plate: short white with green text
jp-c2hu.summary: Short white plates with green text. Light cars (Kei cars) have short yellow plates with black text.

jp-cX54.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image)

jp-cwwN.title: Bollard: flat white with spaced orange reflectors
jp-cwwN.summary: A flat white bollard with several separated orange reflectors on one side and plain white on the other, on Kyushu and in Yamaguchi. Rare ones in Hokkaido have orange on both sides.

jp-f6X5.title: Language: kanji plus looped hiragana
jp-f6X5.summary: Japanese mixes kanji (like Chinese characters), hiragana (simpler, soft and looped) and katakana. Signs mostly use kanji and hiragana.

jp-fWHC.title: Driving side: left
jp-fWHC.summary: Traffic drives on the left. Hong Kong does too; South Korea and Taiwan drive on the right.

differs.how: South Korea drives on the right

jp-g6M6.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image)

jp-iauQ.title: Bollard: white with round reflectors
jp-iauQ.summary: Usually simple white bollards with round reflectors on top. Sometimes black or with extras, and some have the city or prefecture written in kanji.

jp-j00C.title: Guardrail: green bands
jp-j00C.summary: Green bands on guardrails are most common in Oita and Miyazaki, but found across Kyushu.

jp-kk8b.title: Plants: bamboo, more in the south
jp-kk8b.summary: Bamboo grows more in the south and thins out going north. Use it only to help narrow the region.

jp-lm-3283.title: Pole plate: Energia written in Latin letters
jp-lm-3283.summary: Chugoku plates usually say Energia in Latin letters and sometimes have a logo.

jp-lm-3285.title: Pole reflector: 6 small ones joined by a strip
jp-lm-3285.summary: Shikoku reflectors have 6 small reflectors with a little strip connecting them in the middle.

jp-lm-347.title: Pole plate: round-cornered
jp-lm-347.summary: The Chubu plate has a rounded shape and can be spotted from far away.

jp-lm-349.title: Pole plate: logo with 4 dots
jp-lm-349.summary: The Shikoku plate has a distinct logo with 4 dots, one for each prefecture.

jp-lm-350.title: Pole plate: silver horizontal, logo top right
jp-lm-350.summary: In Hokuriku, plates are silver and horizontal with the logo at the top right. NTT plates are also horizontal (in Tohoku they are vertical).

jp-lm-351.title: Pole plate: silver horizontal, logo top left
jp-lm-351.summary: In Tohoku, plates are silver and horizontal with the logo at the top left. NTT plates are vertical.

jp-lm-352.title: Pole reflector: grey-white or grey-yellow
jp-lm-352.summary: Tohoku pole reflectors are grey-and-white or grey-and-yellow.

jp-lm-354.title: Guy wire: paddle-shaped
jp-lm-354.summary: Guy wires shaped like a paddle are unique to Kyushu and Okinawa.

jp-lm-355.title: Pole plate: silver, handwritten, 3 digits
jp-lm-355.summary: The Kanto plate is often silver with handwritten characters: horizontal characters above three vertical digits.

jp-lm-356.title: Pole plate: many numbers in rows of two
jp-lm-356.summary: The Hokkaido plate has a lot of numbers in rows of two.

jp-lm-358.title: Pole reflector: tall with washed-out colours
jp-lm-358.summary: A tall reflector with washed-out colours is exclusive to Kansai.

jp-lm-360.title: Pole: black hat on a white insulator
jp-lm-360.summary: Kanto insulators have a black hat on top of a white insulator.

jp-lm-3602.title: Road diamond: skinny, Kung Fu salute pattern
jp-lm-3602.summary: A skinny painted road diamond in a pattern like a Kung Fu salute points to Shizuoka.

jp-lm-3603.title: Road diamond: small, skinny, broken middle
jp-lm-3603.summary: A snack-size skinny painted diamond that is broken in the middle points to Saga.

jp-lm-3604.title: Road diamond: small, four overlapping clockwise
jp-lm-3604.summary: A small painted diamond of four pieces overlapping clockwise points to Nara, mostly the north.

jp-lm-3605.title: Road diamond: skinny, four counter-clockwise
jp-lm-3605.summary: A skinny painted diamond of four pieces overlapping counter-clockwise points to Yamanashi and Nagano.

jp-lm-3606.title: Road diamond: full size, two overlapping Ls
jp-lm-3606.summary: A full-size painted diamond with two L shapes overlapping clockwise on the wide angles points to Aomori.

jp-lm-3607.title: Road diamond: full size, Kung Fu salute pattern
jp-lm-3607.summary: A full-size painted diamond in a Kung Fu salute pattern points to Kagawa.

jp-lm-3608.title: Road diamond: full size, four clockwise
jp-lm-3608.summary: A full-size painted diamond of four pieces overlapping clockwise points to Nara and Wakayama.

jp-lm-361.title: Pole plate: logo, 3 numbers, kana plus 3 numbers
jp-lm-361.summary: The Kyushu plate has a distinct logo (sometimes missing), three numbers across the top and four vertical characters below on the right: one kana and three numbers.

jp-lm-363.title: Pole reflector: protruding bumps
jp-lm-363.summary: Reflectors with protruding bumps, sometimes a darker reflector in the middle, in Kyushu and Okinawa.

jp-lm-364.title: Pole plate: numbers with lines, often 2+ plates
jp-lm-364.summary: The Okinawa plate has several numbers with lines between them, and often more than two plates.

jp-lm-613259.title: Pole: bulky black meteor-like insulator
jp-lm-613259.summary: A bulky, black, meteor-like insulator in Kyushu. It looks like Kanto's black-hat insulator from afar but is chunkier.

jp-lm-660632.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image) (no description of the design)

jp-lm-660640.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image) (no description of the design)

jp-lm-660642.title: Road diamond: thin, < shape
jp-lm-660642.summary: A thin painted diamond shaped like < points to Nagano or Shizuoka.

jp-lm-660643.title: Road diamond: thin, full
jp-lm-660643.summary: A thin full painted diamond points to Nagano, Aichi, Yamaguchi or Kagoshima. Only meaningful when thin; the thick one is everywhere.

jp-lm-660644.title: Road diamond: thick, clockwise
jp-lm-660644.summary: A thick painted diamond with a clockwise pattern points to Gunma, Gifu or Chiba.

jp-lm-660645.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image) (no description of the design)

jp-lm-660646.title: Road diamond: thin, top left
jp-lm-660646.summary: A thin painted diamond with a piece at the top left points to Ishikawa or Kumamoto.

jp-lm-660647.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image) (no description of the design)

jp-lm-660652.title: Road diamond: small, top right
jp-lm-660652.summary: A small painted diamond with a piece at the top right points to Hiroshima or Tokushima.

jp-lm-660654.title: Road diamond: thick, top left
jp-lm-660654.summary: A thick painted diamond with a piece at the top left points to Mie or Kochi.

jp-lm-660657.title: Road diamond: thick, top right
jp-lm-660657.summary: A thick painted diamond with a piece at the top right points to Miyagi, Kyoto, Hyogo or Okayama.

jp-lm-660659.title: Road diamond: thick, horizontal
jp-lm-660659.summary: A thick painted diamond with a horizontal pattern points to Tottori, Shimane or Saga.

jp-lm-660660.title: Road diamond: small, horizontal
jp-lm-660660.summary: A small painted diamond with a horizontal pattern points to Saga.

jp-lm-660661.title: Road diamond: thick, counter-clockwise
jp-lm-660661.summary: A thick painted diamond with a counter-clockwise pattern points to Nara or Wakayama.

jp-lm-660662.title: Road diamond: thin, clockwise
jp-lm-660662.summary: A thin painted diamond with a clockwise pattern points to Yamanashi.

jp-lm-660663.title: Road diamond: thick, < shape
jp-lm-660663.summary: A thick painted diamond shaped like < points to Kagawa.

jp-lm-660664.title: Road diamond: thick, double top right
jp-lm-660664.summary: A thick painted diamond with two pieces at the top right points to Oita or Toyama.

jp-lm-660666.title: Road diamond: thick, double top left
jp-lm-660666.summary: A thick painted diamond with two pieces at the top left points to Niigata, Tochigi, Ibaraki, Saitama or Okinawa.

jp-lm-660667.title: Road diamond: thin, double top left
jp-lm-660667.summary: A thin painted diamond with two pieces at the top left points to Niigata or Ibaraki.

jp-lm-679878.title: Guy wire: yellow with a flat black lid
jp-lm-679878.summary: Kyushu and Okinawa guy-wire covers are yellow with a flat black lid in the middle.

jp-lm-679879.title: Guy wire: orange-yellow with a low bulge
jp-lm-679879.summary: Chugoku guy-wire covers are orange-yellow with a large bulge near the bottom.

jp-lm-679880.title: Guy wire: bottle-shaped, black-yellow stripes
jp-lm-679880.summary: Kansai, Hokuriku and Shikoku guy-wire covers are bottle-shaped with black and yellow stripes.

jp-lm-679881.title: Guy wire: wide black-yellow stripes
jp-lm-679881.summary: Chubu and Okinawa guy-wire covers have wide black and yellow stripes.

jp-lm-692532.title: Road arrow: silver bolts around the edge
jp-lm-692532.summary: An edge-of-road arrow with silver bolts around the border, found in Aomori and more rarely Hokkaido.

jp-lm-692533.title: Road arrow: long and thin
jp-lm-692533.summary: A long, thin edge-of-road arrow, found in Gifu.

jp-lm-692534.title: Road arrow: yellow and black, northern highway
jp-lm-692534.summary: An alternate yellow-and-black arrow on the northern part of National Highway 275 in Hokkaido.

jp-lm-692535.title: Road arrow: yellow and green
jp-lm-692535.summary: A yellow-and-green edge-of-road arrow found southwest of Sapporo.

jp-m8Ow.title: Language: katakana, simple angular shapes
jp-m8Ow.summary: Katakana is used mainly for foreign words and is common in adverts. It uses simple, geometric shapes, less artistic than hiragana and kanji.

jp-mGDI.title: Landscape: farm fields with red soil
jp-mGDI.summary: Red-soil farm fields are common on several southern islands, mostly Miyakojima and Ishigaki in southern Okinawa.

jp-nAl0.title: House: hot water, gas or propane tanks
jp-nAl0.summary: Hot water, gas and propane tanks are more common in the north and in high mountainous areas, in several shapes.

jp-nLH3.title: Plants: tea hedges with frost fans
jp-nLH3.summary: Green tea grows in hedged rows, with fans on poles to keep frost off. Shizuoka (36%) and Kagoshima (34%) grow most of it.

jp-nPKQ.title: Pole: orange and black bands around the pole
jp-nPKQ.summary: Orange-and-black bands wrapped around poles are often found in Shikoku.

jp-ndLI.title: Pole: transformer, lamp-shaped insulators
jp-ndLI.summary: In Hokuriku, transformers attach with thin metal bars and often have small lamp-shaped insulators; no other bar. Niigata uses the Tohoku design instead.

jp-or2V.title: Route marker: hexagonal prefecture shield
jp-or2V.summary: Prefecture roads use hexagonal shields, often with the prefecture in kanji under the number. Different prefectures reuse the same road numbers.

jp-p0xY.title: Bollard: striped cover, no reflectors
jp-p0xY.summary: Striped bollards that cover the original, with a thinner top half and no reflectors, common in Tohoku and especially Akita.

jp-p58z.title: Landscape: two flat plains
jp-p58z.summary: Japan is very mountainous, but the Nobi and Kanto plains are flat. They can look alike, and telling them apart helps.

jp-pNOF.title: Plants: giant butterbur leaves by the road
jp-pNOF.summary: Giant butterbur (called cabbage) is abundant in Hokkaido and some northern prefectures, with smaller leaves further south. It grows along roadsides. Sakhalin, Russia also has it, but not with a low camera.

differs.how: Russian Sakhalin has no low-cam coverage

jp-qIFc.hide: no learnable content (generic text; the clue is only in the image)

jp-sWrH.title: Pole: transformer on square with bottom bar
jp-sWrH.summary: In Kansai, a straight or zigzag bar sits at the bottom of a square with the transformers on its sides, occasionally on a vertical bar. Tohoku's bar is on top.

jp-sdRS.title: Road: tiny circles that spray warm water
jp-sdRS.summary: Snow-prevention roads (Shosetsu) have tiny circles in the pavement that spray warm groundwater to melt snow, mainly on the northwest coast.

jp-tF8q.title: Sign: Cyrillic writing
jp-tF8q.summary: Cyrillic appears on signs in Wakkanai and Nemuro, in northern Hokkaido.

jp-tSNC.title: Pole: top with four thick bars and a circle
jp-tSNC.summary: A pole top with four thicker bars and a circle at the top is common in Chubu.

jp-tsJL.title: Pole: 120-degree angled arm
jp-tsJL.summary: Attachments with an angle of about 120 degrees are common on poles in Kansai. Sometimes just an arm angled downward.

jp-uFy4.title: Bollard: two yellow stripes, one round reflector
jp-uFy4.summary: In Aomori: two yellow stripes, a single round reflector, and extendable. Sometimes just one thicker stripe near the top.

jp-um29.hide: no learnable content (generic note about architecture styles)

jp-vpIU.title: Pole: cross bar, half triangle, hat insulators
jp-vpIU.summary: In Shikoku, a cross-shaped bar in the middle on a half triangle, with hat-shaped short horizontal insulators. A white sticker with black numbers is often under the transformer.

jp-wVGg.title: Bollard: octagon top, red stripe, sloped base
jp-wVGg.summary: Octagonal reflector with a red stripe under it and a sloped joint between base and reflector, exclusive to Okayama.

jp-wcDd.title: Road: bike lane, white outside, blue inside
jp-wcDd.summary: Cycling routes in Ehime have white on the outside and a blue line inside, more common along the coast. Rare exceptions exist elsewhere.

jp-wtVB.title: Houses: Shisa guardian lions and house plaques
jp-wtVB.summary: Shisa guardian lions and house plaques with special characters are found in Okinawa. Colours and shapes vary.

jp-xUOO.title: Houses: white concrete with flat roofs
jp-xUOO.summary: Okinawa often has white concrete buildings with flat roofs.

jp-y6He.title: Houses: flat roofs and ladders in the north
jp-y6He.summary: Further north, roofs change from tile to flat or low slope for heavy snow, and houses often have a ladder on the side for clearing snow. Snowy mountain areas elsewhere do the same.

jp-yMq5.title: Guardrail: chevron-like stickers
jp-yMq5.summary: Chevron-like stickers, more rarely orange, on guardrail ends and sides, on metal posts between wire fences, and on bridge railings in Hokkaido.

jp-yYkM.hide: content only in the image (kanji list); text has no usable detail

jp-ydq3.title: Pole: painted like birch trees
jp-ydq3.summary: Artistically painted poles that look like birch trees are unique to the city of Date in Hokkaido.

jp-yru1.title: Sign: black with two yellow circles
jp-yru1.summary: Black signs with two yellow circles are found in Kagawa, sometimes stacked or with an arrow above.

jp-zkIK.title: Pole: short reflector, yellow or white stripes
jp-zkIK.summary: Reflectors on poles are short and don't touch the ground, with yellow vertical or diagonal stripes, or white stripes. Taiwan's diagonal stripes reach the ground; South Korea's are thicker.

differs.how: South Korea's diagonal stripes are thicker
